title: Kedarnath Disaster — Extreme Rainfall & Chorabari Lake Breach
hazard: Extreme rainfall → moraine-dam breach → debris flood
region: Chorabari Tal → Mandakini valley, Rudraprayag District, Uttarakhand
detectedChange: Chorabari Lake moraine dam breached; lake drained and never reformed
changePct: 315 mm rain in 24 h at the WIHG Chorabari camp
summary: Two events, not one. On the evening of 16 June 2013 torrential rain in the Saraswati and Dudh Ganga catchments sent a debris-laden flood through upper Kedarnath and completely destroyed Rambara. At 06:45 IST on 17 June the moraine dam of Chorabari Tal, about 2 km upstream of the temple, gave way and released a second, larger flash flood down the Mandakini through Gaurikund, Sonprayag, Guptkashi and Agastyamuni. The lake did not reform: the moraine was largely washed away. Roughly 300,000 pilgrims were in the region at the peak of the Char Dham season and there was effectively no warning.

mparams.label: Glacier Geometry
mparams.source: Chorabari Glacier sits in a cirque some 6 km wide with meltwater flowing down a narrow steep-sided valley (Wikipedia/Chorabari Lake, citing Negi) — verified description; area figure approximate.

mparams.label: Ice / Snow
metrics: Rapid melt of Chorabari Glacier snowpack
mparams.source: WIHG glaciologist D.P. Dobhal (via Dialogue Earth, "Death of Chorabari lake"): incessant rain and rapid snowmelt raised the lake level by seven metres — verified as reported.

mparams.label: Crack & Instability
mparams.source: Wikipedia/Chorabari Lake and Dialogue Earth: on 17 June 2013 the moraine gave way; the lake did not reform because much of the moraine had been washed away — verified.

mparams.label: Glacial Lakes
mparams.source: Coordinates and the ≈2 km upstream position from the Chorabari Lake record — verified. Lake area is an approximate pre-event figure.

mparams.label: Hydrology
metrics: 16 Jun, 17:15 IST — Saraswati / Dudh Ganga flood
mparams.source: Shri Kedarnath Charitable Trust (Uttarakhand Govt.) chronology of the two events with times — verified.

mparams.label: Weather / Climate
mparams.source: Mehta et al. via ResearchGate for the camp totals; Dialogue Earth for the 315 mm/24 h WIHG record — verified as published.

mparams.label: Terrain
mparams.source: Published analyses attribute much of the Gaurikund destruction to narrowing of the river course slightly upstream — verified narrative; slope value approximate.

mparams.label: Infrastructure
mparams.source: Route length from Dialogue Earth/PreventionWeb; damage costs as compiled by ecologist C.P. Kala — verified as reported, converted figures.

mparams.label: Exposure
mparams.source: Government of Uttarakhand figures as reported: >5,700 presumed dead including 934 local residents, toll later placed at 6,054 — verified as reported. The ≈300,000 stranded figure is widely cited but approximate.

mparams.label: Response Resources
mparams.source: Reconstructed from published accounts of the response. Specific base and helipad locations are approximate; there was, as reported, effectively no warning and most people were taken by surprise.
